claims.supportedWording: Municipal real-property taxes are a first-priority lien that need not be registered.
Proceedings may begin after the statutory one-year timing point and property must be put up after three preceding fiscal years, subject to exceptions and deferral.
The process includes preliminary notice, title search, possible survey and a sixty-day notice of intent to owners and interest holders.
The sale or tender receives at least thirty days of qualifying public notice.
Public auction is the default; council may consent to tenders and may define an acceptable minimum.
The statute controls payment forms, requires an immediate price or recovery deposit and gives three business days for any balance.
CBRM's July 2026 event uses in-person registration, bidding cards, immediate minimum-plus-fee payment and a three-business-day balance.
Municipalities may use public tenders, and Kings policy contemplates livestreamed opening.
A listed parcel may be paid, redeemed, removed or deferred before or during the event.
Inverness's August 11, 2026 Port Hood auction requires immediate recovery-amount plus $200 recording payment and a three-business-day balance.

claims.supportedWording: Dated Nova Scotia examples use open auction, sealed tender, post-auction tender and no-sale-year practices within the statutory framework.

claims.supportedWording: Minimum bid is a recovery number; 24 CBRM March 2026 sales had a median winning/minimum ratio of 3.17.

claims.supportedWording: Richmond's June 2026 results publish three sold rows at approximately 1.33, 6.59 and 6.28 times listed charges.
Full payment produces a certificate of sale that the treasurer registers.
The certificate holder may protect and non-diminishingly use the land, may collect rent, must avoid injury and tree cutting and must insure insurable buildings.
Redemption normally lasts six months, but no right exists when taxes were more than six years in arrears at sale.
Redemption uses a statutory formula including purchase price, ten-percent annual interest and specified approved costs and offsets.
On full redemption payment, the purchaser is repaid under the statute and loses rights in the land.
The tax deed vests fee-simple title free of encumbrances, subject to the statute's continuing easement and right-of-way treatment.
A treasurer may obtain a court order defining arrears, interests, notice and protected sale terms.
Surplus proceeds enter a municipal account and prior interest holders may apply to Supreme Court after redemption and before twenty years.
AAN identifies the assessment account and PID identifies the parcel; neither proves boundaries, access or permitted use.

unresolvedConflicts.question: When does HST apply?
unresolvedConflicts.conflict: CBRM states an event-level rule for vacant/commercial property while CRA treatment depends on transaction facts.

unresolvedConflicts.question: What can a purchaser do with an occupied property?
unresolvedConflicts.conflict: The certificate statute grants protective and rent powers, but possession and tenancy consequences depend on facts and separate law.

unresolvedConflicts.question: What interests survive a tax deed?
unresolvedConflicts.conflict: Provincial deed-effect language is broad but unexamined federal, Indigenous, environmental, utility or statutory interests cannot be resolved generically.

unresolvedConflicts.question: What does immediate deed mean?
unresolvedConflicts.conflict: It removes the six-month statutory redemption period but does not establish immediate possession, insurance, development permission or physical certainty.
